correctness.rationale: Reconstructed the 1992 integral homology generators a,b from the original page image. The explicit invertible mod-2 change T intertwines both generators with the even-weight S5 module W. The alternating dot pairing and standard theta characteristic parity establish q(A,B)=|A∩B| mod2. Stabilizer fixed-space analysis proves End_S5(W)=F2, so the full orthogonal commutant on W+W is GL2(F2)=S3. Multinomial orbits and their S3 bundle structure are exhaustively proven; packaged stdlib verifier runs 256 pairs and reproduces exact 14 S5 orbits and six S3 orbit bundles. No lift to geometric automorphism is claimed.

originality.rationale: The already known 120/136 orbit-size lists and the existence of the integral symplectic commutant are not claimed as new. The evaluated claim is the explicit parity-compatible pair-of-even-subsets realization and the commuting S3 action on all fourteen orbit classes, giving a structural reason for four triples noted as unexplained in the 2023 primary publication. Direct source/statement comparisons did not find this precise action; there is a genuine residual priority risk because the group-theoretic ingredients are older.
residual_risks: Riera–Rodríguez 1992 already provides an integral symplectic commutant; the abstract existence of its mod-two S3 shadow is consequently implicit and not claimed novel.
A previous representation-theoretic note, unpublished calculation or indexing omission may already describe the induced S3 permutation of theta-orbit triples.
The proposed S3 is only a finite orthogonal symmetry; neither a curve automorphism nor a polarization-preserving abelian-variety automorphism is established.

value.rationale: The 2023 Bring curve primary paper explicitly calls the repeated 5/10/20/30 theta orbit sizes a threeness without satisfactory explanation. A finite quadratic S5-module identification and its exact S3 commutant explain four triples by a structural group action, rather than recomputing known counts. This is a natural, complete explanation of a named gap for one of the most symmetric genus-four curves, within the carefully limited 2-torsion scope.
